transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I started putting together a memorial for my brother, and it’s gotten much bigger than I intended. I’ve been spending most of my days finding songs, calling people, planning displays and trips. My wife says I’ve put aside the garden, my walking group—pretty much everything else.
Besides being busy with the memorial planning, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable, or that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy?

Yeah. I get very fired up about it, like I’m full of purpose and this memorial is going to make the whole town understand our family. But then, if my wife or somebody at the senior center questions something or slows things down, I can snap at them pretty quickly.
How long has this stretch of feeling extremely energized, needing less sleep, and feeling this intense sense of purpose about the memorial lasted so far—days, or weeks?
It’s been about two months now, ever since my brother passed and I started working on the tribute.

Before this current period, have you ever had episodes in the past where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable for a stretch of time, or times when you felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things for weeks or more?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time that stands out like this.
Have you ever gone through a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down, lost interest in things you normally enjoy, or felt unusually low on energy, even if it wasn't extreme?
I don’t know. I can’t really recall a period like that lasting a couple of weeks.

During these past two months, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or holding beliefs—like special powers or a special mission—that others found unusual or untrue?

Sometimes when I’m at the kitchen table sorting through his song sheets, I hear my brother behind me—humming, or telling me which tune comes next. It sounds clear as day, but when I turn around, nobody’s there. Nobody else in the house hears it.
Has anyone in your close family—like a parent, sibling, or child—ever been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, manic-depressive illness, or had noticeable episodes of extreme mood swings?
Not that I know of. I can’t recall anyone in my close family having those kinds of mood swings or being diagnosed with anything like that.
